description.narrative:
The Youth 2030 project will advance the dimensions of the HCA programme related to youth governance and participation by utilising UN-Habitat’s in-country presence in Cali, Thies, Tamale, Da Nang, Jaipur and Quito. Furthermore, the project will engage the expertise of HCA country project leads as well as youth-led organisations and youth representatives within the HCA programme and network to support the implementation of key project deliverables. UN-Habitat will draw on the expertise and resources of its partners in HCA countries and utilize this multistakeholder approach to catalyze city-wide mobilization of young people engaged in NUA and SDGs focused initiatives.
Youth 2030 will create an enabling environment for young people to engage in governance and participate in and evidence to policy process, which will entail sharing their experiences in youth-led sustainable urbanization and building on and developing programmatic and policy models from those. These dialogues with young people will occur through the organization and implementation of Youth 2030 Urban Forums led by UN-Habitat and HCA representatives in its countries of operation as well as Ecuador. These forums also aim to integrate its key outcomes and DeclarACTION into National Urban Forums and Policies, regional and global activities, including WUF11. These efforts will add a distinct focus on youth in sustainable urbanization, assuring that the concerns and recommendations of young people are represented and integrated in all high level processes.
In addition to specific countries’ outcomes, a global survey will be undertaken, expanding upon the Global Children and Young People’s Wellbeing Survey2, informing and framing the outputs and products of this initiative. The new survey will, using the health and wellbeing lens, take a deeper look into youth and governance, ensuring inclusion of marginalized voices from a global perspective in line with the principles of E2A and Agenda 2030, “leaving no one behind.” The survey will also explore how youth-led organizations operate to carry out key interventions related to the NUA and SDGs and to get a better understanding of the challenges they face during the process. These findings will help with efforts to build the capacity of youth-led organizations for long-term operation and sustainability, while taking into consideration their diverse needs and realities.
The Youth 2030 Urban Forums will be held over 2 days at the national level and will have a similar modality to that of the WUF Youth Assemblies, bringing together approximately 100 young people from each city. These young people will go through a process in which they will learn from each other and from in-country and global experts brought in virtually, on issues pertaining to inclusive sustainable urbanization. In addition to learning about urban sustainability issues, they will develop a Global DeclarACTION on Young People and Sustainable Urbanization for their country. The Global DeclarACTION will become the roadmap for urban youth action within that country, relating to the achievement of the SDGs and the NUA. If there is a National Urban Forum or Policy process, Youth 2030 will link them to this process, assuring that their concerns and recommendations become an integral part of urban policies and discourses. If no formal process exists, the outputs of the Forums will be used to kick start a dialogue on urbanization within that country.
The development of national Compendiums, along with the DeclarACTIONs will ensure the views and actions of young people are recognized in forums such as the Quito +5 High Level Forum. The Compendium and DeclarACTION stand on their own and are also cumulative, meaning that they represent the needs and aspirations of the young people in the country they originate, but as well are brought together in a global Compendium and a global DeclarACTION. Other high-level events that this process will feed in to are the Innovate4Cities Conference (October 2021), the High-Level Meeting on Implementation of the New Urban Agenda (April 2022), the ECOSOC Youth Forum and the International Youth Conference. The Global Compendium and DeclarACTION combined for all 6 countries will be presented at the WUF11 Youth Assembly and shared widely at WUF11.
To support the work of young people leading up to and following the Youth 2030 Urban Forums, a virtual Community of Practice (COP), developed by UN-Habitat in partnership with young people, will be launched in parallel which will allow continued networking and development of their experiences into best practices and models. On this platform youth leaders and youth-led organizations will also be able to access a Youth Governance Scorecard tool. Training for this tool will be done during the Forum, utilizing this to hold their governments accountable on issues of urbanization, for example, the provision of safe public space.
